title: Time bound for an increment call
statement: Let $I$ be a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine and let $j$ be a natural number. Suppose that on every Boolean input $u$, machine $I$ halts within $j(|u|+1)$ steps and outputs the fixed-width increment of $u$, using the empty word when that increment overflows. Then for any Boolean words $x$ and $s$, there is a time $t\le (j+3)(|s|+1)$ at which the buffered composition of the assembly machine with $I$, started in its candidate phase with $s$ on its first work tape and input $x$, is halted and has output equal to the fixed-width increment of $s$, with overflow represented by the empty word.
hypotheses_covered: For every Boolean input, $I$ computes the defaulted fixed-width increment within $j(|u|+1)$ steps
replaced:
Suppose a machine $I$ computes, within time $j(n+1)$ on inputs of length $n$, the
output word of the fixed-width binary increment (the successor word, or the empty
word on overflow). Then from the candidate seam in the candidate phase with
candidate $s$ on input $x$, the buffered composition of the assembly machine
with $I$ halts within $(j+3)(|s|+1)$ steps and outputs the increment result of
$s$, which is empty exactly on overflow.
